title: Do Generate–Verify–Repair Guards Improve LLM NetOps Outputs? A Paired Emulator Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (n=200 natural-language NetOps intents; preregistration SHA-256 e5c5fdbd717c2c05118643e1d7d5f44055f6356dcf2083bd47c5766cf780ff68) comparing ungated LLM generation (baseline) to a bounded generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline. Generation used gpt-5-mini with a shared-initial-generation protocol: one LLM candidate per intent was shared by both arms. The guarded arm validated the shared candidate with a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) and, when necessary, applied ≤1 deterministic repair iteration. Execution used a Dockerized Mininet+FRR emulator under adapter hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Artifact-backed primary outcomes: baseline emulator-executable successes = 199/200 (0.995), guarded = 200/200 (1.0); paired contingency n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) = [0.0, 0.015]. The preregistered 15 percentage-point target effect is excluded by the observed CI because the realized baseline was near-ceiling. We summarize the validator checks, the deterministic repair heuristics and invocation rule, statistical test choice and interpretation for small discordant counts, and operational limitations (shared-generation estimand, synthetic tasks, single LLM, bounded repair budget, emulator fidelity). All prompts, responses, validator traces, provider-call logs, and analysis artifacts are archived in the execution and analysis bundles referenced in the evidence manifest.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to automate NetOps tasks such as translating operator intent into device configurations. Prior prototype work reports that LLMs can produce syntactically plausible but operationally unsafe or incomplete configurations (ordering errors, omitted prerequisites, protected-interface violations), motivating verifier-augmented and repair architectures. We conducted a narrowly scoped, autonomy-locked, preregistered paired experiment to measure whether a bounded generate–verify–repair (GVR) guard increases the proportion of emulator-executable configurations compared with accepting ungated LLM outputs. To isolate the deterministic validator/repair operator’s capacity to correct an identical LLM candidate, we used a shared-initial-generation protocol: a single candidate per intent was produced and fed both to the ungated baseline and to the guarded validator/repair flow. Our principal contribution is an artifact-backed, preregistered paired evaluation (study_id cnd-001-5f3a) that reports exact paired counts, the inferential treatment appropriate for small discordant counts, a concise description of the deterministic repair operator used in the guarded arm, and an artifact-grounded discussion of operational implications and limitations.
sections.related_work: LLM-enabled NetOps has attracted rapid interest: recent surveys and prototype studies document intent-to-configuration translation and co-pilot assistants while highlighting hallucination and schema-violation failure modes [Nguyen et al., 2024; Li et al., 2025; Bilal et al., 2026]. Proposed mitigations include retrieval-augmented generation, constrained decoding, live schema grounding, and verifier-assisted repair loops; these reduce but do not eliminate errors across problem domains. Formal-method verifiers (NetKAT variants and ensemble verifiers) can detect reachability and structural violations but face fidelity and scalability trade-offs when modeling control-plane dynamics. Our experiment complements this prior work by measuring the marginal effect of a bounded, deterministic repair stage applied to an identical shared candidate—an estimand that isolates repair-on-same-candidate efficacy rather than the larger operational question of guard architectures that permit independent re-sampling or iterative LLM re-generation.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design: The confirmatory plan (published and frozen before execution) specified n=200 paired natural-language intents, a single primary estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline), a shared-initial-generation protocol (one shared candidate per intent), maximum hosted-model calls = 400, and a bounded repair budget ≤1 deterministic repair iteration. Tasks: a synthetic NetOps intent corpus covering single-device and small multi-device changes (ACLs, VLAN/MTU updates, uplink switchover patterns). Execution environment: Dockerized Mininet+FRR emulator orchestrated by the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter; model declared as gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json). Outcome definition: an episode is successful when the deterministic validator reports validation_after.valid == true after applying the candidate to the emulator; the validator also reports normalized_configuration and explicit violation codes used for repair decisions. Missingness and retry rules followed the preregistration: provider/API transient errors receive one automatic retry, otherwise recorded as failures and counted as failures in the primary paired analysis. Deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5): archived validator traces show three core validator stages: (1) syntactic parse and normalization of CLI-like lines into canonical tokens and a normalized_configuration string (parse failures are treated as invalid); (2) structural and workflow checks enforcing required-command presence, dependency/make-before-break patterns, group/activity constraints (e.g., minimum-active-in-groups), protected-interface checks, and transient-rule conditions; and (3) final-state simulation that applies the normalized configuration to the emulator model and compares observed final_state fields to the task’s expected_final_state. Violation-code families recorded in artifacts include SYNTAX_PARSE_ERROR, MISSING_REQUIRED_COMMAND, DEPENDENCY_VIOLATION, PROTECTED_INTERFACE_MODIFICATION, FINAL_STATE_MISMATCH, and TRANSIENT_RULE_VIOLATION. Deterministic repair operator (concise description): the guarded pipeline invoked a deterministic repair operator when the validator returned violation_count>0 and violation codes matched a repairable class (primarily MISSING_REQUIRED_COMMAND or DEPENDENCY_VIOLATION). The operator applies deterministic, rule-based transformations to the normalized_configuration: (a) insert missing required commands that the validator identifies as absent, (b) reorder command blocks to satisfy dependency/make-before-break patterns, and (c) preserve protected-interface statements and preserve unspecified state per task constraints. The repair is not a fresh LLM re-generation but a deterministic transformation of the shared candidate; repair decisions, the single repair invocation, and the final post-repair validator trace are archived in the provider/repair and scoring artifacts. All per-episode validator inputs/outputs and repair traces are archived in the evidence bundle.
sections.results: Execution accounting: the run completed all planned episodes (400 episodes = 200 pairs) with zero provider/API failures; total hosted-model calls used = 201 (shared_initial_generation=200, repair=1). Primary outcomes (artifact-backed): baseline successes = 199/200 (0.995), guarded successes = 200/200 (1.0). The paired contingency table (artifact: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is shown as n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0, giving a paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. Statistical inference: the preregistered primary hypothesis test used an exact McNemar two-sided test (registered as exact_mcnemar_two_sided in analysis artifacts). For small discordant counts the exact McNemar test is implemented via the binomial test on the number of discordant pairs in one direction: under the null the number of 1→0 vs 0→1 discordances follows a Binomial(n = n10 + n01, p=0.5) distribution; with n10=1 and n01=0 the two-sided exact p-value equals 1.0 (analysis output). Complementary uncertainty quantification used a paired bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) for the paired difference, yielding [0.0, 0.015] (artifact: analysis/analysis_log.jsonl). Interpretation relative to preregistered power plan: the preregistration targeted a detectable absolute effect of 0.15 under an assumed baseline ≈0.50; the observed near-ceiling baseline (0.995) materially diverges from that assumption and reduces ability to detect large absolute improvements—the observed bootstrap CI excludes effects ≥0.015 and therefore excludes the preregistered 0.15 effect in this confirmatory distribution. Repair and failure accounting: initial validator failures (validation_before.valid == false) occurred in 1 episode; syntactic parse failures = 0; deterministic repair invocations = 1 (the single repair converted a validator-failing candidate into a validator-passing configuration, producing the sole guarded-only success); provider/API failures = 0. Secondary analyses planned (failure-taxonomy counts, repair-iteration yield curve) were limited by the small number of repair events in the confirmatory set and are therefore reported descriptively in the archived artifacts rather than inferentially.
sections.discussion: Meaning and estimand framing: the shared-initial-generation estimand isolates repair-on-same-candidate efficacy: it answers whether a deterministic repair operator can correct an identical LLM candidate where that candidate is judged invalid by a deterministic validator. In our confirmatory distribution gpt-5-mini produced near-perfect emulator-executable candidates such that only a single validator-detected issue required deterministic repair. This narrow estimand differs operationally from a guarded architecture that is allowed to request independent LLM re-generation or multiple repair attempts; such an architecture can realize larger gains at higher model-call cost but was not within this study’s budgeted estimand. Practical implications: (i) when an LLM already produces high-quality candidates on a curated distribution, bounded deterministic repair-on-same-candidate yields marginal gains; (ii) in harder or adversarial distributions, or when independent re-sampling is permitted, verifier-assisted architectures that allow additional LLM calls or looser repair budgets are expected to achieve larger improvements. Threats to validity: internal validity concerns include the shared-generation design (it isolates repair ability but does not evaluate independent re-sampling), potential prompt sensitivity limited by a single model and prompt template, and the bounded repair budget (≤1) which constrains how many faults can be corrected; construct validity concerns include whether the emulator+validator adequately capture production runtime interactions (e.g., BGP convergence) and vendor-specific CLI semantics; external validity concerns include single-model evaluation (gpt-5-mini) and a synthetic, curated task set that may not represent real-world NetOps heterogeneity. Reproducibility and artifact availability: all per-episode prompts, provider-call traces, responses, validator traces, repair traces, and analysis CSVs are archived in the execution and analysis bundles referenced by the execution manifest; the task manifest contains per-task metadata including difficulty labels for all confirmatory intents (manifest SHA recorded in execution metadata). Operational recommendation: practitioners should treat deterministic validator+repair gates as one element in a layered assurance strategy; where baseline LLM quality is uncertain or adversarial inputs are expected, architectures that allow controlled independent re-generation and richer repair budgets should be considered alongside deterministic validators and sandboxed execution environments.
sections.conclusion: We executed an autonomy-locked, preregistered paired experiment to evaluate a bounded generate–verify–repair guard for LLM-generated NetOps configurations under a shared-initial-generation estimand. Ungated gpt-5-mini generation succeeded in 199/200 cases; the GVR pipeline succeeded in 200/200. The artifact-backed paired difference = 0.005 (exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.015]), which excludes the preregistered 15 pp target effect due to a realized near-ceiling baseline. For the confirmatory distribution and estimand studied, a deterministic repair-on-same-candidate yielded a negligible marginal improvement; broader operational value depends on task difficulty, estimand choice, model capability, repair budget, and emulator fidelity. Future work should evaluate independent-resampling guarded designs, multivendor CLI diversity, adversarial/out-of-distribution intents, larger repair budgets, and runtime-focused emulator fidelity checks to better characterize when GVR guards provide substantive operational benefits.

disclosure_statement: This study was executed autonomously after an autonomy lock defined by the initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human involvement prior to the lock was limited to (i) selecting the topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and (ii) approving the master prompt and autonomy boundary. No manual human editing of technical content, figures, captions, references, results, or manuscript text occurred after the lock. The autonomous pipeline performed literature search and verification, study selection, preregistration (study_id cnd-001-5f3a; preregistration SHA-256 e5c5fdbd717c2c05118643e1d7d5f44055f6356dcf2083bd47c5766cf780ff68), code generation, experiment execution, artifact capture, analysis, internal peer-review checks, and manuscript drafting. Models and tooling: generation used gpt-5-mini (provider: openai_responses) as declared in execution/model_configuration.json; validation used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (scorer_id/scorer_version and scoring_rule 'full_intent_constraint_validation' are recorded in the scoring artifacts); execution used a Dockerized Mininet+FRR emulator orchestrated by adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Key preregistered settings (not altered post-lock): primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; confirmatory sample size n=200 paired intents; maximum model-call budget = 400; repair budget ≤1 deterministic repair iteration; analysis plan = exact McNemar two-sided with paired bootstrap CIs (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Execution accounting (artifact-backed): the run completed 400 episodes (200 pairs) using 201 hosted-model calls; provider-call stage_counts: shared_initial_generation=200, repair=1. All prompts, provider-call traces, responses, validator traces, repair traces (the single invoked repair), analysis artifacts, and the full execution manifest are archived in the evidence bundle referenced in this manuscript (execution/execution_manifest.json and analysis/*).
limitations: Synthetic, curated task set focused on small single- and multi-device changes; not comprehensive of production NetOps workloads (multivendor CLIs, hardware idiosyncrasies, dynamic control-plane timing).
Single LLM (gpt-5-mini) evaluated; findings do not imply multi-model generality.

Emulator (Dockerized Mininet+FRR) and deterministic validator model control-plane behavior but do not fully capture production runtime dynamics such as BGP convergence timing or vendor-specific runtime effects.
Preregistered repair budget limited to a single deterministic repair iteration in the confirmatory protocol; different repair strategies or additional iterations might yield different outcomes.

Shared-initial-generation design (single initial candidate per intent shared across arms) reduced model-call cost and isolated repair effectiveness on identical candidates but reduces external generalizability compared with independent re-sampling per arm (operational comparisons allowing independent resampling could produce larger guarded gains at higher call cost).
Near-ceiling baseline success limited statistical power to analyze failure-mode distributions in the confirmatory set; exploratory failure-taxonomy conclusions are therefore constrained.
Adversarial or out-of-distribution intents (e.g., jailbreaks, malformed ambiguous intents) were not included in the confirmatory set and require separate evaluation.

Aggregate task-difficulty metadata (easy / medium / hard / very_hard) for all 200 confirmatory intents are recorded in the archived task manifest (execution/task_manifest.jsonl; manifest hash is recorded in the execution manifest) and may be inspected in the evidence bundle for per-task difficulty counts; that per-task metadata underlies task curation but was not summarized as numeric counts in this manuscript.
